name: tutorial-steps-visual
description: Step-by-step visual walkthrough of all 23 tutorial steps (0-22) with per-step screenshots for visual regression testing. Exercises the tutorial overlay from start through congratulations, capturing each step's UI state, highlight targets, and progress indicator. Every player-facing step is a real click gated by the tutorial's own rail (issue #479/Finding #74 follow-up), including the box-cut and haul-debris stages the file originally skipped entirely.

expect.note: #553: cash bumped from tutorial_pit's own $80,000 (Level.ts) to $202,824 -- drilling became queued, vehicle-gated work, so this file now pays for a driving_center, a driving.drill_rig course and a tier-1 drill_rig it never used to ($52,780 together), and burns 400 ticks of payroll, fuel and maintenance ($70,044) while the lone driller sinks the 9-hole pattern. The bump is exactly those two, so every cash figure from the drill wait onward is the pre-#553 schedule unchanged. #554: bumped again to $218,824 -- charging is real work too now, and the charge order's own wait step burns more payroll/fuel before the freight_warehouse purchase further down this file, which came up $10,126 short at the old figure. #554-followup (issue #586 CI): bumped once more to $224,000 -- switching the charge-drain wait from chunked tick-N rounds to a single giant tick 225 (see that step's own note, fixing a real interaction-mode deadlock) burns marginally different real fuel/payroll than the chunked version did over the identical 225-tick span, and the freight_warehouse purchase further down came up ~$2,534 short at the old figure. #555 (this merge): bumped again to $300,176 -- dig_ramp_segment is now gated the same way, so this file also needs a driving.excavator course and a rock_digger ($52,500 together) plus the extra payroll/fuel/maintenance drain of the real ticks box-cut now spends actually digging instead of completing in the same tick it was ordered, applied on top of the #554-followup $224,000 baseline; re-verify against an actual run.

steps.description: issue #585: tutorial_start now has a real command-mode implementation too (createRunner.ts), pausing the game the same way the browser boot path (main.ts) always did -- command mode used to report "Unknown command" here and never start anything; now both modes genuinely set state.isPaused = true. The added waitForSelector/waitForTutorialStep only run in interaction mode (command mode has no DOM to wait on) and gate every real click below on the rail actually being armed, mirroring tutorial-interactive.json.

Command-mode-only unpause (issue #585): with tutorial_start now genuinely pausing (see its own step above), tickCommand's own loop stops after exactly one real tick while paused regardless of the requested count -- every bare `tick N` below (survey wait, training waits, drill/charge waits, haul wait) would silently advance only 1 tick without this. Interaction mode's own waitForTutorialStep-driven steps run their own real clock independent of console pause state, so this resume has no effect there.

Result unaffected: nothing downstream reads survey findings by location, only the flat $3,000 survey cost. tutorial_start (step 2) arms the tutorial rail (tutorialStages.ts): a control not on the current stage is inert, so every player-facing step below is a real click gated by waitForTutorialStep, matching tutorial-interactive.json's proven pattern.

Issue #716: replaces the four hand-measured `tick 10` blocks (40 ticks total) this step used to be. The seismic survey ordered above actually completes at tick 14 (direct trace: 'Advanced 10 tick(s). Now at tick 10' then '[tick 14] seismic survey complete'), so 26 of those 40 ticks were pure idle padding with nothing left to wait on -- and idle ticks are not free: the surveyor (employee #1) is the same employee who later becomes the box-cut/drill-plan digger (trained driving.excavator further down), and every idle tick between finishing the survey and being handed a real task drains their hunger/fatigue against SitePolicy's own continuous-mode thresholds (60/60, applied at the set-early-policy step below) with nothing to show for it. Direct trace confirmed this padding was the root cause of #716's box-cut deadlock: with it in place, employee #1 starts the walk to board the rock_digger already below both thresholds, SitePolicy's shouldForceRest fires almost immediately (activeActionId gates it while idle, so this only bites once they're finally given real work), interrupts the walk, and each interruption releases the vehicle reservation (interruptActiveAction, GameLoop.ts) -- forcing a full walk back to re-board on top of the rest itself. The cycle compounds (repeated interruptions crash morale to 0 and fatigue to 100 before a single ramp segment is ever dug), so the box-cut stage's own isComplete (a ramp nav-cell count increasing) never fires within the wait's budget. `waitUntil` on `surveyCount` (mirrors `createComparisonStep`'s own `surveyResults.length` check, tutorialSteps.ts) stops the instant the survey actually lands instead of guessing a fixed tick budget -- matching this file's own #689-followup precedent for the drill/charge waits further down.

#681: set-early-policy complete -- the tutorial's new step 3a-ii. Continuous still forces rest on hunger/fatigue (shouldForceRest checks that in every mode), just without the shift-length cap. The later set-policy step (unchanged) still teaches shift_8h once the grind is over.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:3 spacing:3 depth:6 start:20,20 diameter:0.089
steps.description: #553: confirming the grid now only ORDERS the 9 holes -- drill_hole became queued, vehicle-gated work, so they are ghosts until the driller drives the rig to each one, and the tutorial does not advance to `charge` until they have landed. The wait is the step below; the mid-pattern screenshot above is the ghosts-and-real-holes picture #553 asks for. Start corrected from the file's original 15,15 to 20,20 (Finding #74/#75 follow-up): the tutorial's drill-plan stage gates its picker to REGION.drill (tutorialStages.ts). #601-followup: REGION.drill is actually `{ x1: 20, z1: 20, x2: 26, z2: 26, exact: true }` -- the prior Finding #74/#75 note here claimed a larger grid and hole count than the tool actually produces, which was never real: a direct `drill_plan show` probe after the real drag+confirm read back spacing 3m but only a 3x3/9-hole grid landing at (20,20)-(26,26), matching REGION.drill's own real x2/z2 exactly, not the wider rectangle the note assumed. `dragTiles`'s x2/z2 corrected from 30,30 to 26,26 (the requested corners get clamped to `exact: true`'s own gate regardless, but the declared numbers should say what the gate actually allows, not a rectangle a real player's drag will never produce) and the command's rows/cols corrected from 4/4 back to 3/3, restoring this file's own original 9-hole declaration. spacing and depth both corrected from the file's original 5/8 to the grid tool's real defaults 3/6 (DEFAULT_SPACING_M/DEFAULT_DEPTH_M, Drill.ts), discovered live: neither stepper (#bs-param-strip [data-field="spacing"|"depth"]) is one of this stage's own targets (tutorialStages.ts's 'drill-plan' entry lists only the toolbar, grid-tool button, and picker canvas/confirm) -- the tutorial rail's own CSS lockout makes every other control pointer-events:none while a stage is active. CI cash mismatch fix: this command was also missing `diameter:`, the established diameter-omission bug (Finding #52 class) -- command mode defaults to 0.15 while the real Drill panel always sends DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M=0.089 (Drill.ts), and computeDrillHoleDurationTicks (DrillPlan.ts) scales hole duration by diameter/0.15, so the omitted-diameter command mode this file's cash values were derived from kept the drill_rig busy (and paying fuelCostPerTick) longer than a real click would. Added `diameter:0.089` to match the real click; every downstream checkpoint through the blast step was re-derived from command mode with the fix applied.

#689-followup: 1/8 of the drill wait, converted from a fixed `tick 50` chunk to a `waitUntil` on holeCount itself. The fixed 8x50=400-tick budget (see this file's own prior #681 note, preserved below on the final chunk) ran to completion regardless of how long drilling actually took -- direct trace against this file's current command sequence (build_ramp/drill_plan exactly as declared, with the current build-living-quarters at 18,14) shows all 9 holes land by tick 216, ~184 ticks earlier than the fixed budget's tick ~400 landing. Those extra ticks were not idle-and-harmless: two employees with nothing to do still drain hunger/fatigue/morale every tick (needsMoraleEffect, EmployeeNeeds.ts), and running ~300 more ticks than necessary before charging even starts was enough on its own to crash wellBeing to 0 and trigger a real worker_revolt at tick 715 -- reproduced identically regardless of living_quarters position (13,4 or 18,14), so the fixed-tick padding itself, not commute distance, was the remaining cause. Stopping the instant holeCount reaches its target removes the wasted ticks; direct trace of the resulting shorter trajectory reaches the charge/sequence/blast stretch below with wellBeing comfortably positive and no revolt.

expect.note: #555 regression guard: the box-cut+drill-plan stretch above is ~250+ ticks of two employees' continuous vehicle-gated work with no living_quarters anywhere in this file's own script -- exactly the pacing that drove wellBeing to a permanent 0 and a worker_revolt game-over here before this fix (ScoreManager.ts's applyDecay had a dead zone at exactly 0: nothing but a strictly positive per-tick delta could ever move a score pinned at the clamped floor, and LevelDef.scoreDecayRate was declared per-level -- tutorial_pit's own 0.01, documented "player-proof" -- but never actually reached updateScores, which always ran the hardcoded global 0.05 instead). Asserting levelEndReason stays null right here, before charge/sequence/blast ever run, is what keeps a future pacing stretch from hiding a revolt behind this file's own closing `campaign complete` debug override again. #681 follow-up: `LevelDef.revoltImmune` (which used to make tutorial_pit immune to worker_revolt outright) is gone -- this block now has to survive the real rules, which is why it is split into eight `tick 50` steps instead of one `tick 400` (see 1/8 above).

steps.description: charge complete: Charge All Holes clicked. This step's own explosive/amount/stemming already match the Charge panel's real defaults (boomite/5kg/2m, confirmed throughout this suite's Finding #10 audit) so the click reproduces the declared command exactly, unlike most other files' charge steps. tutorial_start (step 2) arms the tutorial rail (tutorialStages.ts): a control not on the current stage is inert, so every player-facing step below is a real click gated by waitForTutorialStep, matching tutorial-interactive.json's proven pattern.

#689-followup: converted from a fixed `tick 225` block to `waitUntil` on chargedCount itself, same reasoning as the drill-wait chunks above -- direct trace shows all 9 holes charge by tick 363 (147 ticks from when charging starts), ~78 ticks short of the fixed 225-tick budget this step used to always spend regardless. Combined with the drill-wait fix above, the full drill+charge stretch now finishes at tick 363 instead of 715, comfortably clear of worker_revolt's own wellBeing-driven countdown.

sequence complete: Auto Sequence clicked. delay_step:25 already matches the Sequence panel's own default (Sequence.ts DEFAULT_DELAY_STEP_MS) so 0 stepper clicks are needed. tutorial_start (step 2) arms the tutorial rail (tutorialStages.ts): a control not on the current stage is inert, so every player-facing step below is a real click gated by waitForTutorialStep, matching tutorial-interactive.json's proven pattern.

blast complete: Execute clicked, confirm dialog answered, Blast Report closed. deathCount raised 1 -> 2 (#558 full-disc survey claim follow-up, issue #558/PR #569): step 5's `survey seismic x:23 z:23` claims its full SURVEY_COVERAGE_RADIUS=20 disc (siteExpansion.ts's cellsInDisc), growing the site from the starting 32x32 to 48x48 before the driller is hired at step 10. Employee hire's spawn point is `minX + sizeX/2, minZ + sizeZ/2` -- on this run minX/minZ stay 0 throughout (the site only grows eastward/southward from (0,0), never crosses into negative territory), so that formula numerically equals the pre-#571 `sizeX/2` here; this scenario's deathCount reproduces identically whether or not the #571 origin-offset fix is applied and is NOT evidence for that fix (verified live, both ways). The real driver is #558's site growth alone: on the grown 48x48 site the spawn point resolves to (26, 24), which lands on the real 3x3/spacing-3 drill grid's own footprint (x:20-26, z:20-26) -- x=26 sits exactly on the grid's east edge, z=24 well inside it. (The prior write-up here cited a furthest-throw distance for a drill grid size that was never real -- see the drill_plan step's own #601-followup note -- so that figure is dropped rather than restated unverified for the real grid.) cash is unaffected either way (lawsuits/fines from a death do not deduct immediately). The #571 origin-offset regression itself is covered separately by the unit/integration tests added in 75a06cf, which force a negative origin (x:-4, z:-4). CI cash mismatch fix: cash corrected 70320 -> 70648 (+$328) now that the drill_plan step above carries `diameter:0.089` -- command mode's own drill_rig spent less time (and fuelCostPerTick) sinking all 9 holes once its duration matches what a real click always produced, so more cash survives to this checkpoint. #553-followup (issue #586 CI): that +$328 offset was correct relative to command mode, but the box-cut step several steps up this same file also turned out to carry a real-time-accrual error that compounds forward -- dropped the exact cash figure here too rather than chase a second moving target. Not replaced with `decreased`: as the note above already says, cash is unaffected by this step in either mode (command mode's own trace shows it completely unchanged), so there is no single mode-agnostic cash claim to make -- holeCount/chargedCount/sequencedCount/deathCount remain exact since they are not host-timing-sensitive. #555 tutorial worker-revolt fix: a real fix, not a route-around -- the preceding box-cut/drill-plan stretch used to crash wellBeing to a permanently-pinned 0 and flip `state.levelEndReason` to `worker_revolt` before this step ever ran (ScoreManager.ts's `applyDecay` had a dead zone at exactly 0, and `LevelDef.scoreDecayRate` -- tutorial_pit's own 0.01, documented "player-proof" -- had never actually reached `updateScores`, which always used the hardcoded global 0.05 instead). Both are fixed now: `state.levelEndReason` stays null through this step and for the rest of the run, `BlastReportModal` opens and renders normally post-blast (its `state.levelEndReason !== null` guard never trips), and this step is back to a real click sequence identical to tutorial-interactive.json's own proven blast step -- `report-close` is genuinely reachable again, not a permanent dead end. #689-followup: deathCount corrected 2 -> 1 now that the drill/charge waits above are `waitUntil`-driven instead of fixed-tick padded (see those steps' own notes) -- the shorter, real trajectory reaches this blast ~350 ticks earlier (tick 363 instead of 715), and the surveyor (Walt Dusty), who used to still be wandering toward the grid by the old, much-later blast tick, is instead idle near the relocated living_quarters (18,14) and survives; direct trace confirms them alive at (17,17). Kurt Hardhat (driller) still dies at the grid-centre spawn point, same mechanism as before -- only the surveyor's fate changed.

#555 tutorial worker-revolt fix (this PR): restored to a real dialog interaction, matching tutorial-interactive.json's own event-choose step -- the `worker_revolt` game-over this used to route around (UIManager.update() defers EventModal while `state.levelEndReason !== null`) no longer fires (see the blast step's own note), so the scripted `tutorial_synergy_consultant` event dialog is genuinely reachable and answerable again, not a permanent dead end.

The file's original decreased:["safety"] assertion does not survive across both modes (Finding #74/#75 follow-up, discovered live) -- not because the point is wrong, but because it is no longer independently checkable here.
